title: Ventilation, cabinets and specialist zones
audience: Cleaners working in laboratories and specialist zones where ventilation and enclosures are used.
learningOutcomes: Explain why airflow equipment and controlled enclosures are not disturbed by routine cleaning.
Confirm exclusions with the equipment owner before housekeeping nearby.
Decline a request to move a cabinet or clean inside a live fume hood, and redirect it to the owner.

instruction.heading: Why airflow and enclosures are treated as equipment
instruction.body: Ventilation equipment, cabinets and fume hoods control airflow and contain materials. An exhaust grille, a supply vent, a fume hood or a biological safety cabinet does its job by moving air in a particular direction at a particular speed, and by keeping a barrier between the people in the room and whatever is being worked on inside. A cleaner who wipes a grille, moves a cabinet, blocks a vent with a trolley, or leans into an open hood can change that airflow without knowing it. The effect can expose people nearby, disturb the work inside the enclosure, or affect the readings that the owner uses to decide whether the equipment is working. The equipment is therefore treated as a fixed boundary, not as ordinary furniture. Routine housekeeping in these zones is limited to what the owner has approved in writing, and anything the owner has not approved is excluded by default.

instruction.heading: Confirm the exclusion diagram before you approach
instruction.body: Confirm the current equipment exclusion diagram with the engineering or laboratory equipment manager before any housekeeping near the equipment. The diagram should show the fume hoods, cabinets, vents and grilles, the no-touch margins, the services that run to the equipment, and any points where a cleaner must not stand or place a trolley. Compare the diagram with the room, and check the date and the version. Find the approved local procedure for the zone, and distinguish what is permitted from what is only assumed. An assumption is not a permission. Permission given by a colleague in a hurry is not permission either, unless it is confirmed by the owner in writing. If the diagram and the room do not match, the room is treated as changed, and you stop until the owner confirms the scope.

instruction.heading: Changed condition and uncertain hazards
instruction.body: When a staff member proposes moving a cabinet and cleaning near a live fume hood, note the difference between the original job and the changed condition. The original job was housekeeping on the approved surfaces. The changed condition involves moving equipment, which may disconnect or strain services such as power, gas, water or exhaust ducting, and may place the cleaner close to an open hood. Any uncertain hazard stops the task, and an uncertain hazard includes a hood whose sash position is unclear, a cabinet with a warning label, an alarm or indicator that is showing, or any service that is not on the diagram. Decline the request to move the cabinet or clean inside a live fume hood, and redirect it to the equipment owner, who decides on a revised scope. Do not adjust the sash, switch a control, or try to make the equipment safe for cleaning. Those decisions belong to the equipment owner and to people trained for them.

instruction.heading: Recording and returning
instruction.body: Make a minimal record of the zone, the observable condition, the excluded task, the responsible contact, the time and the follow-up. Describe what you saw in plain words, such as a cabinet with a lifted panel or an open hood with items on the work surface, without assuming why. Resume only after the site authority gives an updated scope and the cleaner is trained and equipped for it. The handover covers housekeeping only, and it never implies sterilisation or contamination clearance. A handover that says the zone is safe, certified or sterile is a claim the cleaner cannot prove. The Australian Competition and Consumer Commission states that claims must be accurate and based on reasonable grounds, that a business must be able to prove its claims, and that statements by staff are covered by the same rule. This lesson does not grant any licence, certificate, plant-safety approval or specialist authority, and completing it does not make a cleaner a specialist.

instruction.heading: Worked boundary: a cabinet, a hood and a request to help
instruction.body: A laboratory has a mobile cabinet beside a fume hood. The hood is in use, and a research assistant asks the cleaner to shift the cabinet a short distance so the floor under it can be mopped, and then to wipe the front of the hood while the sash is open. The request has three parts, and each is handled separately. The mopping is in scope only if the diagram shows the floor between the cabinet and the hood as open, and the cleaner can confirm that with the owner. Moving the cabinet is excluded, because it may disturb services and the airflow around the hood, and the decision belongs to the owner. Wiping the front of an open hood is excluded because it is a live enclosure, and the sash and the work surface inside are not in the cleaner's scope. The cleaner declines the move and the hood work, redirects both to the owner, records the request and the changed condition, and asks for a written decision on the floor. If the owner confirms only the floor, the cleaner mops only that floor, with the cabinet left where it is.

procedure: Confirm the equipment exclusion diagram and its version with the equipment manager before any housekeeping near the equipment.
Find the approved local procedure and separate permission from assumption. Permission from a colleague is not permission unless the owner confirms it in writing.
Stop any task where the scope has changed, a hazard is uncertain, or a service is not on the diagram.
Decline any request to move a cabinet or clean inside a live fume hood, and redirect it to the equipment owner.
Do not adjust sashes, switch controls, block vents or grilles, or lean into an open enclosure.
Record the zone, the observable condition, the excluded task, the contact and the follow-up.
Resume only with an updated scope from the site authority, and clean only the areas it names.
Describe the handover as housekeeping only, with the exclusions listed and no claim of sterility or certification.

workedExamples.situation: Staff propose moving a mobile cabinet and cleaning near a live fume hood, so the floor under the cabinet can be mopped.
workedExamples.decisionPrompt: What do you do, and what is the changed condition?
workedExamples.reasoning: Decline the move and the cleaning inside the live fume hood. The changed condition is that the job has moved from housekeeping on approved surfaces to moving equipment near an open enclosure, which may disturb services and airflow. Redirect the request to the equipment owner, who decides any revised scope. Record the request, the people involved, the time and the decision, and leave the floor under the cabinet until the owner confirms it in writing.

workedExamples.situation: A fume hood has its sash open with items on the work surface, and a colleague asks the cleaner to wipe the outside of the hood frame while they are there.
workedExamples.decisionPrompt: Is the frame in scope, and what do you record?
workedExamples.reasoning: Check the diagram first. If the frame is not listed as an approved surface, it is excluded, and the cleaner does not reach into or lean over the open hood. If the diagram does list the frame and the owner has confirmed it in writing, the cleaner may clean only the listed frame from outside the enclosure, without moving the items inside. Record the sash position as it was seen, the items on the work surface, the decision and the time. Do not record the hood as cleaned unless the frame was in scope and was cleaned.

workedExamples.situation: A cleaner finds a grille on the wall of a laboratory covered by a loose cardboard box, which may have been placed there to block the noise.
workedExamples.decisionPrompt: Do you move the box, and what do you record?
workedExamples.reasoning: Do not move the box if it is the only thing touching the grille, because moving it could change the airflow and the owner needs to see the condition as it was. Record the grille's location, the box and the time from a safe distance, and report it to the equipment manager. The grille is excluded from the housekeeping, and the equipment manager decides whether the box is removed and by whom.

equipmentAndPpe: Exclusion diagram from the equipment manager, with its version date and the no-touch margins marked.
Deferral record form with fields for zone, observable condition, excluded task, contact, time and follow-up.
Gloves as set by the site procedure, and only products approved for the surface, with the safety data sheet available.
Eye protection where the approved product's safety data sheet or the site procedure requires it.
Personal protective equipment is a last resort after higher-level controls such as keeping clear and not reaching into the enclosure.

commonErrors.error: Moving a cabinet because a colleague asked, or because it is in the way of the floor.
commonErrors.prevention: Only the equipment owner authorises a changed scope. Decline and redirect the request.

commonErrors.error: Cleaning inside a live fume hood, or leaning into an open enclosure to reach a corner.
commonErrors.prevention: Stop. Fume hoods are excluded unless the owner has authorised the work in writing.

commonErrors.error: Blocking a vent or grille with a trolley, box or cleaning cart.
commonErrors.prevention: Keep trolleys and boxes clear of vents, grilles and the front of the enclosure.

commonErrors.error: Telling the client that the laboratory is sterile or that the enclosure is certified.
commonErrors.prevention: Describe only the housekeeping done, and never imply sterilisation or certification.

commonErrors.error: Adjusting a sash or switching a control to make the area easier to clean.
commonErrors.prevention: Do not operate controls. Report the sash or control position and let the owner decide.

safetyAndRegulatory.point: Laboratory work involves biological and chemical hazards. This lesson does not authorise entry to restricted laboratory zones, handling of samples, sharps or instruments, chemical-spill response, biological decontamination, sterilisation, waste treatment or laboratory clearance.

Safe Work Australia describes the hazardous chemicals register as covering hazardous chemicals used, handled or stored at a workplace, with a current safety data sheet for each entry, and readily accessible to workers. Ask for the register entry for any product used near a fume hood or cabinet before you use it.

The Australian Competition and Consumer Commission states that claims must be accurate and based on reasonable grounds, and that a business must be able to prove the claims it makes, including claims made by staff. A statement that a zone is safe, sterile or certified is a claim the cleaner cannot support from housekeeping.
Certification and testing of this equipment are the owner's responsibility, under the owner's method.

qualityStandard: Scope confirmed against the exclusion diagram and its version date in the desk exercise.
Changed condition recognised, and the request declined and redirected in the case study.
Vents, grilles, sashes and controls left as found, with no adjustment by the cleaner.
Record produced with the responsible owner, the observed condition and no clearance claim.
documentationEvidence: Minimal incident or deferral record with zone, observable condition, excluded task, contact, time and follow-up.
Written decision from the equipment owner on any revised scope.
Authorised return criteria from the site authority, before any resumption.
Housekeeping-only handover with exclusions listed and no sterility or certification claim.
summary: Ventilation, cabinets and fume hoods are not disturbed without the owner's written approval.
A changed scope or an uncertain hazard stops the task until the owner decides.
Decline requests to move cabinets or clean live enclosures, and redirect them to the owner.
Never imply sterilisation, certification or clearance.

knowledgeChecks.question: A colleague asks you to move a cabinet near a live fume hood. What do you do?
options: Move it, since the colleague asked and it is a quick job
Decline, and redirect the request to the equipment owner
Move it quickly before the owner arrives on site

knowledgeChecks.question: What should the handover say about a cleaned laboratory zone?
options: That the zone is sterile after the housekeeping was done on the day today
That only the housekeeping done is recorded, with no sterilisation or clearance claim
That the zone is certified safe for use by the next team on the day of the clean

knowledgeChecks.question: When can work resume after a changed condition is found?
options: When the colleague says it is fine to carry on with the job on the day
After lunch, once the team has had a short break and the room is quiet and calm
After the site authority gives an updated scope and the cleaner is trained for it

knowledgeChecks.question: A sash on a fume hood is open and a vent is partly blocked by a trolley. What is correct?
options: Close the sash and move the trolley so the area can be cleaned
Leave the sash and the vent as found, record them, and report to the owner
Lean into the hood to see whether anything is inside
